description: Figure 3 presents a comparison of problem distributions based on correctness, categorized by whether knowledge was included (“w/ KNOWLEDGE”) or excluded (“w/o KNOWLEDGE”), and utilizing Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting. The figure consists of two pie charts, one for the “w/ KNOWLEDGE” setting and one for the “w/o KNOWLEDGE” setting. The “w/ KNOWLEDGE” pie chart is divided into four slices: “Verify-All” (light blue, approximately 65.4%), “N+K” (dark blue, approximately 25.1%), “N+” (light green, approximately 4.7%), and “N” (dark green, approximately 4.8%). The “w/o KNOWLEDGE” pie chart is also divided into four slices: “Verify-All” (light blue, approximately 30.8%), “N+K” (dark blue, approximately 39.6%), “N+” (light green, approximately 9.9%), and “N” (dark green, approximately 20.6%). Both charts include a legend identifying the slice labels and corresponding colors. Percentage labels are displayed inside each slice. The slices in both charts appear to be ordered from largest to smallest, based on their proportional size.
